tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.description:
Control native apps or browsers on the user’s computer by reading or operating UI. Prefer purpose-built skills, connectors, APIs, or CLIs when available.

On the first invocation of `cua_repl`, or after resetting it, execute exactly one of the API calls shown below, optionally assigning its result to a variable. Do not add other API calls, waits, or snapshots to that invocation.
The tool result will include documentation and, when creating or selecting a tab or selecting an app, its initial UI state. Selecting a browser does not open a tab. Read that result before continuing.
Use only APIs described in the tool instructions or returned documentation.

When you need an inventory of available apps, browsers, and tabs, get a snapshot of all enabled surfaces. Otherwise, use the relevant entry point below:

```javascript
await cua.getState();
```

Use the first matching browser control option from the user's request:

For a tab @-mention (`mention=tab-v1`):
Pass the complete `plugin://...` URL to get the referenced tab.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ mention: tabMentionUrl });
```

For an existing tab identified by URL in browser context (including the current IAB tab):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ url }, { browser: browserId });
```

Known tab ID (`tabId` or `providerTabId`) and browser (name or browser @-mention):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: browserId });
```

To open a URL in the in-app browser (`@Browser`):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab("iab", url, { visible: boolean });
```

To open a URL in another named browser: pass its name directly; do not call `getBrowser` first.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab(browserName, url, browserOptions);
```

Known URL, only when the user has not specified a browser by name or @-mention:

```javascript
let browser = await cua.getBrowser({ url });
```

Browser IDs and options:

- `"mcpapps"`: use `cua.getBrowser({ id: "mcpapps" })` for existing full-screen MCP Apps in the task’s side panel.
- `"iab"` (in-app browser): in `createBrowserTab`, use `visible: true` to show the browser; `false` to keep it hidden.
- `"dot"` (Dot): use only when present in browser inventory. It accesses tabs on Dot's active main thread. `cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: "dot" })` selects an existing tab. `cua.createBrowserTab("dot", url, { visible: boolean })` creates one with the same visibility options as `"iab"`.
- `"chrome"` (@Chrome), `"edge"` (@Edge): pass a short, emoji-prefixed `sessionName` (e.g. `"🔎 Task"`) to `createBrowserTab` when starting a task.

If the user specifies an app to use, get the app by name, bundle ID, or path:

```javascript
let app = await cua.getApp("Example App");
```

To add other content to the tool result, use `nodeRepl.write(value)` for text or other values and `await nodeRepl.emitImage(image)` for images. The APIs listed above already display their documentation or UI state; do not wrap their results in `write` or `emitImage`.

If your context begins with a summary of an existing computer use task, call `await cua.rewriteDocumentation()` before continuing the computer use task to ensure you have a complete view of the necessary documentation.

Several `cua_repl.js` calls may work toward the same goal. As soon as you observe the final outcome of the CUA part of the task, your next output item must be a standalone assistant commentary message containing only `::browser-complete{title="<headline>"}`. Emit it exactly once. Do this before using another tool for the next part of the user’s request or sending your reply, even if the overall request continues. If you hand control to the user, wait to summarize until the handoff has ended and you’ve observed the final outcome of the CUA part of the task. Follow the commentary in the same response with your next tool call or final answer.

Write a headline for the observed outcome in three to six words total. Start with a past-tense verb and name the result in plain language, as in 'Booked a plumber for Thursday' or 'Renewed vehicle registration'. Leave identifiers, values, and explanations for the reply. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

code.description: JavaScript to execute using the initialized cua_repl runtime.

timeout_ms.description: Optional execution timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000 (30 seconds) when omitted.

title.description: Short user-facing description of what this code block is doing. Prefer a few words in present-progressive form, such as 'Checking the mobile layout' or 'Comparing prices', over imperative or past-tense titles.

tools.description: Reset the persistent cua_repl JavaScript session. All JavaScript bindings are discarded. The next cua_repl.js call initializes a fresh runtime for the enabled surfaces. Brief: lattice-Boltzmann close-ups for a museum explainer. Is the setup well-posed, and what can we claim?

Context. This is a static website for the Mercedes-Benz Museum. Four exhibits get a precomputed airflow close-up, each showing two cases:
- 190 E Evo II rear-wing flap, down vs raised
- Evo II front splitter lip, in vs 40 mm forward
- Evo II front wheel arch (one state only)
- W 196 R front wheel, enclosed vs exposed

The claims are deliberately small: only the sign of a change, and only if it repeats on two grids. Computing is offline on one 10-core Mac, with our own Node.js solvers: about 16 M cell-updates/s in 2-D and about 30 M/s in 3-D. A fine-grid run takes 1–3 hours.

Numerics, common to both solvers
- BGK collision with Smagorinsky eddy viscosity (C_s = 0.16).
- Half-way bounce-back on the body. The road is a moving wall at u = U, in the car's frame.
- Free-slip top (3-D also free-slip side, and a mirror plane at the centreline).
- Inlet: equilibrium populations at ρ = 1, u = U, imposed every step, so density and velocity are both fixed.
- Outlet: zero-gradient (copies the last interior column).
- Reynolds number is held at a nominal value across grids by scaling ν with the cell size. Statistics: settle for several flow-throughs, then three averaging windows of one flow-through each.

Problem 1 (main): 2-D splitter section (D2Q9)
- Geometry: the centre-plane nose profile, traced from a photo. The body top is at 744 mm and the floor (ride height) at 120 mm; the lip is 25 mm thick. The body runs from the nose through the outlet, so it is effectively semi-infinite.
- Domain: 1.0 m ahead of the bumper face, 1.6 m behind it, 2.5 m tall. The body blocks about 30 % of the height, and the under-floor gap is a 120 mm channel driven by the moving road.
- Parameters: U = 0.1 (Ma ≈ 0.17); Re = 10⁴ on 1 m.
  - 5 mm cells: ν = 0.002, τ = 0.506.
  - 2.5 mm cells: ν = 0.004, τ = 0.512.
- Observations:
  - Pressure level: the interior sits 2–4 q∞ above the inlet density. Three cells behind the inlet there is already a vertical gradient of about 0.9 q∞. Referenced to the mean density at that inlet column (what our live tunnel uses), the lip's upper face reads cp ≈ 1.2 (not physically ≤ 1). So absolute cp is unusable.
  - Drift: the lower-face pressure keeps rising monotonically in every window. Lip in: 0.72 → 0.80 → 0.86. Lip forward: −0.16 → 0.02 → 0.18. The difference across the lip (upper minus lower, which needs no reference) is larger with the lip forward in every window, but that excess shrinks: 0.99 → 0.85 → 0.74. This was after 3 flow-throughs of settling.
  - Failed variant: ending the floor 0.5 m behind the bumper (a step up to 560 mm, open underneath) made the run diverge (NaN) within about 3 flow-throughs.
- Questions:
  a. Is the drift physical (the under-floor channel filling or emptying on a long time scale), or an artefact of the inlet fixing both ρ and u while the outlet pressure floats? Would a velocity inlet with free density (Zou–He), a pressure outlet, or a sponge zone fix the reference and the drift?
  b. What is the minimal well-posed 2-D section for a lip study?
     - Full-length car section with a closed tail and wake, versus a truncated body?
     - How far upstream should the inlet be, and how tall the domain, to keep blockage effects below the case-to-case difference?
  c. Is "upper minus lower face pressure, averaged over a fixed chord interval" a sound proxy for lip load? And is "sign agrees on both grids, and the change beats the drift between first and last window" a defensible stationarity test? If not, what is (a time scale estimate, a batch-means method)?

Problem 2: 3-D front-corner tunnels (D3Q19, half car mirrored)
- Setup:
  - U = 0.08, Re = 10⁴ on the 680 mm tyre diameter.
  - Cells of 24 mm (τ ≈ 0.5007) and 16 mm (τ ≈ 0.501), so the closure does essentially all the dissipation.
  - The tyre is still and lifted 48 mm above the road, so there is no contact-patch staircase; it is only 6–9 cells wide.
  - Domains are about 4.4 × 1.8 × 1.4 m (half width), so blockage is substantial; larger-domain runs are under way.
- Metric: width of the band where the time-mean |u| < 0.8U, on a fixed line at hub height 0.7 m behind the axle.
- Results:
  - W 196 R exposed: 574–806 mm (24 mm grid).
  - W 196 R enclosed: 830–870 mm (24 mm) and 826–858 mm (16 mm).
  - Evo arch: a path seeded in line with the tyre is shifted 377 mm outward at the station (24 mm grid); the three windows read 367–377 mm.
- Questions:
  d. At τ → 0.5 with this resolution, is a two-grid check at fixed nominal Re meaningful? The filter width scales with h, so the effective Re differs. What should be held fixed instead?
  e. Is the wake-width metric robust to blockage and to the still, lifted tyre? Would you pick a different observable for "enclosed vs exposed wheel"?

Problem 3: what to compare
6. Evo arch: the mesh's flared arch already sits at the tyre's outer face, and a narrower arch would expose the tyre, so there is no physical second case. Is there a meaningful variant at this resolution (for example, an open versus closed wheelhouse face), or is a single traced path the honest lesson?
7. Wing: the wing view is a crop of an earlier whole-car run (28 and 40 mm grids). The mean flow direction above the trailing edge goes from −8.6° to +4.0° on the 28 mm grid and from −2.3° to +5.7° on the 40 mm grid: the sign agrees, the size does not. Is a local wing solve with an inlet sampled from the whole-car field worth it, or is the sign the most this geometry (a game mesh) can support anyway?

What we need back: boundary-condition and domain changes for the 2-D section that remove the drift and fix the pressure reference; a defensible stationarity and grid criterion within a budget of a few CPU-hours per part; and a yes or no on whether each claimed sign is supportable.

L25: In order to study the aerodynamic forces and flow features of rotating wheels, compromises and simplifications are often made in wind tunnel testing, and more frequently so in numerical modelling. A CFD approach similar to that commonly used in industry was utilised to investigate common assumptions involving; the influence of geometric fidelity in wheel hub regions, ground representation, the modelling of the contact patch, and the effects of rotation on separation.
L26: It was found that the separation and wake characteristics were strongly influenced by the rotation of the wheel; the separation point changed by as much as 90% compared to a stationary wheel, and drag was close to 20% less – downforce was approximately 40% greater.
L27: In addition, the modelling of the contact patch, treated here as a small step to facilitate skew-free meshing necessary for a reliable converged result, was seen to cause up to a 52% difference in predicted lift characteristics, and an increase in the step of just 2 mm decreased the maximum wake thickness by close to 50% – considerable changes stemming from superficially-minor simplifications.
L28: Including indented wheel hubs proved to be more influential on the production of vortices and wake structures, causing the merging of previously-separate vortex structures. The results point to a need for very careful evaluation of the goals of any study when determining which simplifications can be made in both physical testing and numerical analysis.

L8: Large-eddy simulation (LES) directly solves for large-scale motions in turbulent flow, while modeling the influence of small-scale eddies. *** Add File: research_notes/Museum airflow claim review/parts.md
+# Corner and wing evidence
+
+## Is the grid check meaningful?
+
+### Takeaway
+
+Yes for the sign of a stated observable in this particular modeling sequence when both paired, stationary contrasts and a domain check support it. Two meshes give no numerical convergence order, validated physical Reynolds number or continuum error bound. Keep the nominal molecular Reynolds number fixed.
+
+### Cited findings
+
+- The corner solver fixes 680 mm as the reference length, lattice inlet speed 0.08 and molecular Re 10,000, so molecular ν in lattice units scales as 1/h and τ₀ = 0.50068 / 0.50102. Its actual BGK relaxation depends on the local non-equilibrium stress. It approaches the molecular value in uniform flow even on these coarse meshes. Smagorinsky ν_t scales with (C_s Δ)² times the strain magnitude. A small molecular τ−½ alone cannot establish that essentially *all* dissipation is from the closure. Numerical and wall dissipation remain separate. [Corner parameters](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/tools/cfd/part.mjs:159) [Local relaxation](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/tools/cfd/lbm3d.mjs:89)
+- Explicit-filter refinement with the same physical filter on successive numerical meshes can examine discretization of a common filtered model. Grid-tied LES couples resolution/model and discretization, often non-monotonically. [Bose, Moin and You, original Stanford report](https://web.stanford.edu/group/ctr/ResBriefs08/13_bose.pdf) [Journal article](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.3485774)
+- W 196 tyre nominal width 150 mm = 6.25 / 9.38 cells. The 48 mm gap (7.1% of diameter) is implemented by cutting the bottom of the cylinder, rather than translating the hub upward, yielding 2 / 3 clearance cells. Evo width actually 270 mm and diameter 666 mm, whereas reference Re uses 680 mm for both. [Corner geometry](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/tools/cfd/corner.mjs:19)
+
+### Inferences
+
+- For budgeted robustness, hold physical geometry, contact/gap ratio, rotation ratio, road speed, inlet, outlet, blockage and mirrors, molecular Re, comparable low Mach, probe positions/physical scales and reduced averaging duration fixed. Keep same model and C_s=0.16 for standard h-filtered LES. Do not tune a global effective Re, τ or C_s across meshes to force agreement. If the question is the numerical error of one filtered PDE, decouple numerical h from an explicit physical filter and consistent SGS mixing length on both grids. Changing C_s alone cannot align the two numerical filters. This is a separate experiment that is usually a poor first purchase here.
+- Sample instantaneous τ_eff/ν_t/ν near the wheel, gap and separated shear layer and, ideally, resolved versus modeled dissipation. Look at maximum local Mach and density swings, and voxelized solid masks for fit/comparable physical clearances. If unable to get a robust result, fix resolution/model or choose a lower stated molecular Re and recompute both states on both meshes as a different model.
+
+### Gaps
+
+- No saved eddy-viscosity budget, explicit filter study, rotating-wheel check, model-validation measurement or sampling error for local wing probe; no evidence for a physical drag or axle-load magnitude.
+
+## What does the W 196 width show?
+
+### Takeaway
+
+No present two-grid sign. A coarse-grid descriptive observation is supported: at the chosen station the exposed version has a wider region of slow mean flow. The strip on the enclosed car sits against its flank; the exposed strip trails the tyre. They are distinct features of two body packages.
+
+### Cited findings
+
+- Quoted 574–806 and 830–870 mm are lateral coordinates of band edges. At h=24, window widths are 220, 232, 232 mm exposed versus 44, 40, 40 mm enclosed. Their mean-field display widths are 232 and 40 mm. At h=16, enclosed widths are 24, 32, 32 mm (edge positions start at 826 mm). Snapshot contains no finished fine exposed field or doubled pair in larger tunnel. The run queue schedules only exposed-big at 24 mm. The export reads only the final named case's big run. [24 mm run record](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/tools/cfd/results/w196-wheel.json:11) [16 mm run record](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/tools/cfd/out/w196-wheel/enclosed-16.json:14) [Run queue](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/tools/cfd/out/logs/run3d.sh:5) [Export](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/tools/cfd/part.mjs:211)
+- The metric is speed of the mean vector, |⟨u⟩|, divided by inlet U, using trilinear interpolation, then identifying a connected sub-0.8 band sampled every 4 mm nearest the nominal outer shoulder. Temporal mean speed ⟨|u|⟩ and turbulence intensity would need other statistics. Interpolation requires every one of eight neighbors to be fluid. This excludes near-mask samples. The 4 mm sampling is interpolated, not 4 mm spatial resolution. [Velocity averaging](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/tools/cfd/lbm3d.mjs:88) [Interpolation](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/tools/cfd/volume.mjs:35) [Metric algorithm](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/tools/cfd/part.mjs:186)
+- The exposed and enclosed approximations change nose length, widths, shape, and fender/wheelhouse, not only covering. The body continues through the outlet. W 196 solid masks give projected frontal blockage 20.7% enclosed / 10.3% exposed at 24 mm, found by counting transverse cells with solid anywhere upstream; maximum sectional area ratio 19.9% / 10.3%. At 16 mm the enclosed projected blockage is 20.3%. [Geometry](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/tools/cfd/corner.mjs:7) [Run geometry supplied to solver](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/tools/cfd/part.mjs:162)
+- I recomputed the original W 196 band rule from the three existing saved full mean volumes, varying only cutoff and station. Across nine threshold/station pairs (0.7, 0.8, 0.9 U and 0.6, 0.7, 0.8 m behind axle), the 24 mm exposed band remains wider. At the original station, widths at those three thresholds are 212/232/244 mm exposed and 32/40/56 mm enclosed. Its inner edge at all three thresholds is the first interpolable fluid sample at y=830 mm; its speed is only 0.21U (fine grid first sample y=826, speed 0.23U). The reported 40 mm is under two cells and is clipped by the fluid interpolation mask, not a resolved boundary-layer thickness. The 16 mm full mean has width 28 mm for 0.8. [Sampler](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/tools/cfd/part.mjs:188) [Volume format](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/tools/cfd/volume.mjs:10)
+- Original simulations compared tyre/contact/wheel modeling choices and found wake thickness and separation sensitive to rotation/contact geometry. Original PIV-based investigation gives physical data on rolling wheels. [Diasinos, Barber and Doig](https://digitalcommons.calpoly.edu/aero_fac/151/) [Haag, Blacha and Indinger](https://doi.org/10.20485/jsaeijae.8.1_7)
+
+### Inferences
+
+- Blockage need not cancel between bodies. Run **both** coarse variants at enlarged width/height and adequate inlet/outlet distance; use paired geometry/gap/rotation sensitivity to extend claims beyond the fixed lifted-tyre model. The gap admits spurious throughflow, particularly exposed. The half-car mirror excludes asymmetric global modes. Physical rolling requires appropriate moving-tread BC and a credible contact representation; a spinning staircase alone is a poor validation.
+- For the existing images, describe two separate features and show the common speed scale, plane and body outline. To compare a local wake, average streamwise velocity deficit or integrate [1−⟨u_stream⟩/U_ref]_+ over a predeclared multiple-cell transverse patch that is fluid for both, with common U_ref, normalization and mask. First verify that the proposed patch contains the scientific feature in both. Where it does not, move downstream behind *both* bodies in a finite-body run, or choose the question of wheel shielding and accumulate streamwise momentum exchange specifically on the labeled tyre, using common tyre reference area. A local deficit integral is a local observable and does not yield vehicle drag (pressure, shear, and other fluxes matter). Avoid a fluid patch carved differently in the two cases, which would manufacture a contrast. Threshold, line, grid, wall-geometry and domain checks test distinct effects.
+- The current public copy's “churned air,” inferred straightaway benefit, hard 23/4 cm, and depiction of the tyre turning exceed what this test measures. Historical statements may have independent sources. [W 196 copy](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/stops/w196r/car.js:33)
+
+### Gaps
+
+- The threshold/station postprocessing used complete-field means only. No alternate window-level fields, rotating or ground-contact runs, fine exposed, or paired enlarged-domain result was available at inspection. A new common-patch or tyre-force metric merits its own paired evidence.
+
+## Which arch and wing lessons survive?
+
+### Takeaway
+
+Arch yes as a picture of one model's mean flow; no comparative flare effect or two-grid claim yet. Wing yes as an archived, local, two-grid upward change in mean direction; no validated force, angle magnitude, or proven stationary sign.
+
+### Cited findings
+
+- The arch seed is (1500,780,344) mm, aligned with the outer part of the tyre, and its station is 600 mm behind the axle. The code zeroes the vertical velocity component when integrating this line at fixed hub-height plane. The result is a streamline of the horizontal projection of the mean velocity. It is neither a 3-D mean streamline nor a time-resolved particle trajectory. Its lateral shifts in the 24 mm window fields are +367/+374/+377 mm; the full-mean displayed path is +372 mm. There is no second grid in this corner record. [Config and seed](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/tools/cfd/part.mjs:157) [Station test](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/tools/cfd/part.mjs:202) [Trace rule](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/tools/cfd/volume.mjs:62) [Arch record](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/tools/cfd/results/evo-arch.json:19)

Both are outward for this seed; a material path is not recoverable from one mean field. All tested neighboring seeds 740, 756, 780, 804 and 820 mm reached the station region and moved outward in both traces. The integration retains a last point before the station; production accepts a point at most 20 mm short, so no decimal-millimetre precision is justified. Old whole-car 'arch vs base' masks were identical and cannot supply a counterfactual. [Arch trace](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/tools/cfd/part.mjs:202) [Voxel audit](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/docs/component-cfd-implementation-proposal.md:11)
